Course Registration Rules
The number of credits a student can register for depends on their cumulative GPA.
•Main Semesters (Fall/Spring):
•GPA ≥ 3.0: Up to 21 credit hours (or 8 courses, whichever is greater).
•2.0 ≤ GPA < 3.0: Up to 18 credit hours (or 7 courses, whichever is greater).
•GPA < 2.0: Up to 14 credit hours (or 5 courses, whichever is greater).
•Summer Semester:
•GPA ≥ 3.0: Up to 9 credit hours (or 3 courses, whichever is greater).
•GPA < 3.0: Up to 8 credit hours (or 2 courses, whichever is greater).

Academic System & Duration
•A student moves to the next level after completing 25% (36 credit hours) of the program requirements.
•Levels are defined based on the percentage of completed credits:
•Level 1: 0% to <25%.
•Level 2: 25% to <50%.
•Level 3: 50% to <75%.
•Level 4: 75% to <100%.
•Program Duration
•Minimum: Eight main semesters.
•Maximum: Eight academic years (excluding approved enrollment suspensions). An additional academic year is granted for students enrolled in a minor program

Selecting Your Elective Track
• Students must complete 7 elective courses (21 credit hours).
• At least 5 courses must be chosen from one concentration.
• Four Tracks are available to guide specialization.

Graduation Requirements
To be awarded a Bachelor of Science in Engineering, a student must:
•Successfully complete the required number of credit hours for their major program.
•Achieve a final cumulative GPA of at least 2.0.
•Pass all mandatory courses with zero (0) credit hours.
•Successfully complete the graduation project. Students must pass at least
70%(101 hours) of the program's total credit hours to register for the project.
•Complete the required field training ( 8 weeks)

Field Training
Field training is a mandatory component of the degree.
•Duration: 8 weeks in a relevant industrial or service facility.
•Timing: The training is divided into two parts: 4 weeks at the end of the second level and 4 weeks at the end of the third level.
• Training can be started after passing 26 CHs of the freshman level, provided
that the duration for the training does not exceed two weeks
• In any case, training for a 6-week period at any level is permitted only once
during the study period

Academic Standing
•Academic Warning
•A student is placed on academic warning if their cumulative GPA drops below
2.0 in any main semester.
•Dismissal from Study
•A student may be dismissed for reasons including:
•Having a cumulative GPA below 1.0 after the first three main semesters.
•Having a cumulative GPA below 2.0 for six consecutive main semesters.
•Failing to meet graduation requirements within the maximum study period.

Selecting Your Elective Track
• Students must complete 7 elective courses (21 credit hours).
• At least 5 courses must be chosen from one concentration.
• Four Tracks are available to guide specialization.

Module Registration Rules (Cont.)
Conclusion:
A student has a maximum of four opportunities to pass a module:
•
First registration – includes first sit and resit.
•
Second registration (within the same academic year or the following year at the latest) – includes first sit and resit.
If the student fails after these four attempts, they will be dismissed from the UEL program.

registered. Students are allowed to study one semester or more at UEL with a 10% reduction in the UK tuition fees.

3. Portfolio: Types, Format, and Templates
There are two types of portfolios: lecture-based courses portfolio and project/studio-based courses portfolio that must be revised and approved by the course instructor on the LMS according to the students’ portfolio revision checklist which will be illustrated later in this booklet.
Portfolio templates are published online, and students must follow and submit their portfolios using the template in only one PDF file with the format which will be explained later. Student’s portfolio must contain only summative assessments except the final examination.

Accordingly, he/she can plan well the required submissions ahead.

Assessment & Grading Criteria and the Difference Between
ASU Courses and UEL Modules.

Course Registration Rules
The number of credits a student can register for depends on their cumulative GPA.
•Main Semesters (Fall/Spring):
•GPA ≥ 3.0: Up to 21 credit hours (or 8 courses, whichever is greater).
•2.0 ≤ GPA < 3.0: Up to 18 credit hours (or 7 courses, whichever is greater).
•GPA < 2.0: Up to 14 credit hours (or 5 courses, whichever is greater).
•Summer Semester:
•GPA ≥ 3.0: Up to 9 credit hours (or 3 courses, whichever is greater).
•GPA < 3.0: Up to 8 credit hours (or 2 courses, whichever is greater).
